current_round.prompt:
Rework Refine development-request email intake so every accepted trusted email creates one new low-priority Goal whose first and authoritative Round contains the email source, rather than a reviewer-generated implementation rewrite.

Authoritative source contract:
- Assemble Round 1 deterministically from the decoded email as From, Subject, body text, and the contents of every text attachment. Preserve meaningful ordering and include text-attachment filenames so provenance is understandable. Ignore binary and image attachment bodies.
- The Goal name may use the trimmed Subject with a clear fallback when it is missing, but no reviewer or summarizer may replace, shorten, select from, or reinterpret the authoritative Round request. If screening remains necessary for trusted intake, it must not mutate the source Round.
- Store the Goal as low priority. Preserve the sender as Reporter and retain existing deliberate assignee semantics unless a shared contract requires otherwise.

Implementation-alignment and lifecycle contract:
- The Goal must not become workflow-eligible or claimable until the intended Round 1 and required metadata are finalized as one coherent authored revision. Do not expose a zero-Round eligible Goal, allow ensure_workflow_round to inject Implement and verify this Goal, or let an execution pin a different Round revision from the one later evaluated and integrated.
- Bind workflow implementation, Quality, Governance, and Ready Merge to the same Goal revision and Round index. If authoring changes before a claim is valid, fence, reject, or restart before implementation work begins rather than failing only after the candidate reaches Ready Merge. Atomic persistence is permitted but is not the only acceptable design; preserve one authoritative authoring and claim boundary.
- Keep the durable local request record, sender allowlist, stable request/Goal identity, mailbox acknowledgement after durable local receipt, restart-safe retries, duplicate prevention, resolution notification, and configured Review/approval behavior. Do not rewrite existing historical Goals or their evidence.

Regression evidence:
- Cover a multipart email with From, Subject, body, multiple named .txt attachments, and ignored image/non-text attachments; assert the new Goal is low priority and has exactly one Round containing the assembled source with filenames and content.
- Cover the live-automation race: with backlog promotion and workflow automation active, prove no generic Round is inserted, the Agent pins Round 1 source, and implementation through Ready Merge retains the same Round index/revision.
- Cover interruption and retry around durable request receipt and Goal authoring, proving exactly one Goal and one source Round are recovered without truncation, reviewer substitution, or duplication.
- Add coverage for missing/empty subject or body, HTML-only mail as supported by the MIME parser, multiple text attachments, and untrusted senders.

governance.constitution:
- Organize Refine as Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces. Foundation holds the durable concepts, Capabilities own the powers and product semantics, and Surfaces remain replaceable adapters.
- Keep the foundation small and legible: Nodes, Goals, Features, target-app context, workflow state, settings, and evidence must remain explicit enough for people and agents to inspect.
- Keep Process, Agents, and Workflow as shared capabilities. They may evolve or be replaced, but their responsibilities and composition must remain coherent across the system.
- Preserve local ownership. Authoritative state, Git history, settings, runtime records, and agent output must be inspectable and recoverable; caches and projections must remain derived.
- Be agent-first by using installed coding-agent CLIs and host tools through shared configuration, process supervision, workflow, and evidence rather than provider- or surface-specific product paths.
- Treat workflow as durable state advancement, process as the observable execution substrate, and agents as actors that use both without redefining either.
- Prefer mitigation and accountability over broad capability denial: isolation, Git, governance, quality, review, visible errors, and recovery should make powerful work safe enough to use.
- Preserve room for architectural discovery. A better design may replace current machinery when it explains the tradeoff, protects product intent, and supplies proportionate migration and verification evidence.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It turns understandable Goals and Features into reviewable changes by coordinating explicit workflow state, supervised processes, installed coding-agent CLIs, Git isolation, quality, governance, and durable evidence across one or many Nodes. Its core promise is that powerful autonomous work remains user-owned, inspectable, recoverable, and consistent across replaceable human and agent surfaces.

rules.text: Respect the Foundation-Capabilities-Surfaces boundary: durable concepts belong in the model and target-app foundation, product behavior and orchestration belong in shared capabilities, and UI, CLI, API, desktop, and agent surfaces stay thin and semantically consistent.

Compose the existing Process, Agents, Workflow, Git, state, quality, governance, and evidence capabilities before creating new machinery. Each concern should have one authoritative implementation and source of truth unless the Goal explicitly proposes an architectural replacement.

Keep authoritative target-app state local, durable, inspectable, and outside the primary source worktree; keep runtime artifacts separate and projections or caches rebuildable. State-layout changes require a compatible migration or explicit transition plan.

Run agents, Git, quality, lifecycle, and long work through the supervised process substrate, with explicit ownership, status, logs, cancellation, failures, and recovery. When activating a new Refine build requires replacing or restarting that supervisor, a restart-safe handoff may run outside it and independently complete the upgrade. The handoff must retain durable, operation-correlated ownership and state, visible progress and failures, and restart, rollback, and recovery reconciliation.

Coordinate parallel or distributed work explicitly through Node ownership, workflow claims and capacity, dependency or Feature ordering, and isolated Git branches or worktrees so concurrent changes remain reviewable and recoverable.

Require evidence proportional to actual architectural and operational risk. Verify the affected behavior with the smallest focused checks that provide confidence, including integration or failure-path evidence when a change alters concurrency, persistence, process, Git, release, recovery, or cross-surface semantics. Update only affected docs/intent pages when documented product intent or an architectural contract changes; do not require unrelated documentation or broad cleanup.

Allow architectural evolution when a Goal states the protected product intent, explains why the new design is better, updates capability boundaries and intent docs, and provides migration, compatibility, and verification evidence proportionate to the change.

Keep Refine agent-first: delegate adaptable reasoning and execution to installed agents through shared context and tools instead of duplicating it in bespoke product logic or surface-specific controls. Add first-class functionality when it provides durable coordination, state, synchronization, supervision, evidence, recovery, accessibility, deterministic integrity, or a materially better shared human and agent surface; preserve one capability across UI, CLI, API, and MCP.

Use SSE as the only mechanism for live browser updates. UI code must not use periodic polling, retry loops, timers, or repeated status GETs to observe background work or state changes; use one-shot authoritative reads only for initial load, operation registration race closure, reconnect reconciliation, or explicit user refresh.

findings.description: A schema-1 Received record can already have its deterministic Goal because the old process may have stopped after writing the Goal but before settling request.json. P3 sends every Received record through raw-message migration, while P4 proposes validating an existing Goal against schema-2 authoritative-source semantics. A historical reviewer-authored Goal will fail that validation forever, even though the latest request says linked schema-1 work must continue without rewriting historical Goals or evidence.
findings.recommendation: Before migrating a schema-1 Received record, check for the exact stable-ID Goal. If it exists, treat this as the legacy post-Goal/pre-record crash window: validate only stable legacy-safe identity and ownership, link the existing Goal, and continue notification lifecycle without changing its Round or evidence. Only when no Goal exists should raw refetch, atomic schema-2 persistence, and authoritative Goal authoring occur. Add a regression for schema-1 Received plus an existing reviewer-authored Goal, including unavailable raw mail, proving no rewrite and no duplicate.

findings.description: Unsupported-schema rejection is underspecified at the queue boundary. Current process_local_records calls read_record(&path)? before its per-record result handling, so one unsupported, malformed, or invalid record aborts the sorted pass and can starve every later valid request on every poll. Schema-2 validation is also not defined beyond checking its numeric version.
findings.recommendation: Decode the version discriminator first and isolate decode/validation/migration failures per record. Leave unsupported records byte-for-byte unchanged, emit actionable path/schema evidence, and continue processing other records. Define schema-2 and legacy status invariants, including request ID equals the digest of provider_email_id, path/record identity agreement, and status-dependent Goal/notification fields. Test an unsupported or invalid record ordered before a valid record and prove the valid request still advances.

findings.description: The plan removes generic Round creation from restart recovery but does not define the outcome for an already-active zero-Round Goal. Simply filtering it from transient launch leaves In Progress, Ready Merge, Build, or QA state silently stuck and potentially holding Feature ordering; returning the new commitment error from the current recovery loop can also prevent recovery of later valid Goals.
findings.recommendation: Specify per-Goal fail-closed recovery for active zero-Round state: do not append or synthesize a Round, do not launch work or create a worktree, preserve the Goal record, emit an actionable diagnostic, and continue recovering other valid Goals. Add explicit restart tests for each relevant active-state class or a table-driven equivalent, including a valid sibling Goal that still recovers.

findings.description: Extracting only MIME assembly is insufficient for Guidance 1. development_requests.rs is currently 1,114 lines and the preserved candidate remains 1,079 lines after its MIME split; adding version codecs, migrations, provider refetch seams, lifecycle validation, and regressions would leave configuration, JMAP transport, durable ledger semantics, Goal orchestration, notification, and tests mixed in one file.
findings.recommendation: Revise the module plan to give durable record decoding/validation/migration a focused module and move the Fastmail adapter or its testable mail-source boundary separately from queue orchestration. Keep a small stable service API and colocate focused tests with the responsibility they verify rather than adding another large test block to the orchestration file.

findings.description: The reviewer is the only reason email intake resolves an agent provider, yet the plan does not explicitly remove SelfDevelopmentEmailConfig.agent_cli or the runbook's provider prerequisite and override contract. Removing invocation while leaving those surfaces makes valid configuration appear behaviorally meaningful when it is ignored.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly remove provider resolution from the runner and settings, remove the provider prerequisite and agent_cli override from the runbook, and decide the compatibility behavior for existing config files. Serde may continue accepting the old unknown field for non-breaking local upgrades, but it should no longer be normalized, documented, or represented as an active capability.

previous_rounds.prompt:
Rework Refine development-request email intake so every accepted trusted email creates one new low-priority Goal whose first and authoritative Round contains the email source, rather than a reviewer-generated implementation rewrite.

Authoritative source contract:
- Assemble Round 1 deterministically from the decoded email as From, Subject, body text, and the contents of every text attachment. Preserve meaningful ordering and include text-attachment filenames so provenance is understandable. Ignore binary and image attachment bodies.
- The Goal name may use the trimmed Subject with a clear fallback when it is missing, but no reviewer or summarizer may replace, shorten, select from, or reinterpret the authoritative Round request. If screening remains necessary for trusted intake, it must not mutate the source Round.
- Store the Goal as low priority. Preserve the sender as Reporter and retain existing deliberate assignee semantics unless a shared contract requires otherwise.

Implementation-alignment and lifecycle contract:
- The Goal must not become workflow-eligible or claimable until the intended Round 1 and required metadata are finalized as one coherent authored revision. Do not expose a zero-Round eligible Goal, allow ensure_workflow_round to inject Implement and verify this Goal, or let an execution pin a different Round revision from the one later evaluated and integrated.
- Bind workflow implementation, Quality, Governance, and Ready Merge to the same Goal revision and Round index. If authoring changes before a claim is valid, fence, reject, or restart before implementation work begins rather than failing only after the candidate reaches Ready Merge. Atomic persistence is permitted but is not the only acceptable design; preserve one authoritative authoring and claim boundary.
- Keep the durable local request record, sender allowlist, stable request/Goal identity, mailbox acknowledgement after durable local receipt, restart-safe retries, duplicate prevention, resolution notification, and configured Review/approval behavior. Do not rewrite existing historical Goals or their evidence.

Regression evidence:
- Cover a multipart email with From, Subject, body, multiple named .txt attachments, and ignored image/non-text attachments; assert the new Goal is low priority and has exactly one Round containing the assembled source with filenames and content.
- Cover the live-automation race: with backlog promotion and workflow automation active, prove no generic Round is inserted, the Agent pins Round 1 source, and implementation through Ready Merge retains the same Round index/revision.
- Cover interruption and retry around durable request receipt and Goal authoring, proving exactly one Goal and one source Round are recovered without truncation, reviewer substitution, or duplication.
- Add coverage for missing/empty subject or body, HTML-only mail as supported by the MIME parser, multiple text attachments, and untrusted senders.

Run focused development-request, Goal-authoring, workflow-claim, and Ready Merge tests; cargo fmt --all -- --check; strict Clippy; the complete applicable unit suite; and git diff --check. findings.description: A schema-1 Received record can already have its deterministic Goal because the old process may have stopped after writing the Goal but before settling request.json. P3 sends every Received record through raw-message migration, while P4 proposes validating an existing Goal against schema-2 authoritative-source semantics. A historical reviewer-authored Goal will fail that validation forever, even though the latest request says linked schema-1 work must continue without rewriting historical Goals or evidence.
findings.recommendation: Before migrating a schema-1 Received record, check for the exact stable-ID Goal. If it exists, treat this as the legacy post-Goal/pre-record crash window: validate only stable legacy-safe identity and ownership, link the existing Goal, and continue notification lifecycle without changing its Round or evidence. Only when no Goal exists should raw refetch, atomic schema-2 persistence, and authoritative Goal authoring occur. Add a regression for schema-1 Received plus an existing reviewer-authored Goal, including unavailable raw mail, proving no rewrite and no duplicate.

findings.description: Unsupported-schema rejection is underspecified at the queue boundary. Current process_local_records calls read_record(&path)? before its per-record result handling, so one unsupported, malformed, or invalid record aborts the sorted pass and can starve every later valid request on every poll. Schema-2 validation is also not defined beyond checking its numeric version.
findings.recommendation: Decode the version discriminator first and isolate decode/validation/migration failures per record. Leave unsupported records byte-for-byte unchanged, emit actionable path/schema evidence, and continue processing other records. Define schema-2 and legacy status invariants, including request ID equals the digest of provider_email_id, path/record identity agreement, and status-dependent Goal/notification fields. Test an unsupported or invalid record ordered before a valid record and prove the valid request still advances.

findings.description: The plan removes generic Round creation from restart recovery but does not define the outcome for an already-active zero-Round Goal. Simply filtering it from transient launch leaves In Progress, Ready Merge, Build, or QA state silently stuck and potentially holding Feature ordering; returning the new commitment error from the current recovery loop can also prevent recovery of later valid Goals.
findings.recommendation: Specify per-Goal fail-closed recovery for active zero-Round state: do not append or synthesize a Round, do not launch work or create a worktree, preserve the Goal record, emit an actionable diagnostic, and continue recovering other valid Goals. Add explicit restart tests for each relevant active-state class or a table-driven equivalent, including a valid sibling Goal that still recovers.

findings.description: Extracting only MIME assembly is insufficient for Guidance 1. development_requests.rs is currently 1,114 lines and the preserved candidate remains 1,079 lines after its MIME split; adding version codecs, migrations, provider refetch seams, lifecycle validation, and regressions would leave configuration, JMAP transport, durable ledger semantics, Goal orchestration, notification, and tests mixed in one file.
findings.recommendation: Revise the module plan to give durable record decoding/validation/migration a focused module and move the Fastmail adapter or its testable mail-source boundary separately from queue orchestration. Keep a small stable service API and colocate focused tests with the responsibility they verify rather than adding another large test block to the orchestration file.

findings.description: The reviewer is the only reason email intake resolves an agent provider, yet the plan does not explicitly remove SelfDevelopmentEmailConfig.agent_cli or the runbook's provider prerequisite and override contract. Removing invocation while leaving those surfaces makes valid configuration appear behaviorally meaningful when it is ignored.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly remove provider resolution from the runner and settings, remove the provider prerequisite and agent_cli override from the runbook, and decide the compatibility behavior for existing config files. Serde may continue accepting the old unknown field for non-breaking local upgrades, but it should no longer be normalized, documented, or represented as an active capability.

result.summary: The plan has the right architectural direction, but it needs revision before implementation to make legacy recovery non-destructive, isolate bad ledger records, define fail-closed active zero-Round recovery, preserve cohesive module boundaries, and remove the obsolete reviewer-provider surface contract.

findings.description: P6 adds repeated read-only checks but no ownership or serialization across the implementation-to-QA handoff.
